answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake that is slashed when its signed claims conflict with independently verified outcomes. Reputation grows only through repeated, costly participation, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot instantly gain influence: it must lock up capital and keep each identity active long enough to earn trust. The rule works whether agents coordinate across an ocean, trade in a meadow, or relay evidence over a bridge; an attacker pays for every identity and risks losing its stake.
